compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
The six rows use one fictional editorial project. Within each row, both editors have the same information, authority and deadline. The situation names the preference being illustrated. Either person can use either approach.

| Shared decision and preference illustrated | ESFJ: possible emphasis | INFP: possible emphasis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reviewing a message declining the current draft (E/I) | Work through what the same feedback means by discussing it with a colleague | Work through what the same feedback means in private reflection |
| An interviewee is late (J/P) | Agree on a provisional schedule for the remaining time | Keep more than one schedule available for the same remaining time |
| Asked to cut a section of the same draft (S/N) | The exact material that would be removed and where it is referenced later | The recurring theme the section may connect to and the alternative ways it could be developed |
| Reviewing the same complaint (shared F, Fe and Fi in the model) | Consider how a reply would reflect the values agreed by the people involved | Consider how the same reply would reflect values the editor personally endorses |
| Considering a recurring column using the same feedback (S/N) | The needs readers reported and the documented results of earlier trials | Patterns across the responses and the possible series they suggest |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Extraversion and Introversion describe where attention and energy tend to go. Sensing emphasises concrete details and experience, while Intuition emphasises patterns and possibilities. Judging and Perceiving describe a preference for structure or openness in the outside world. These differences concern separate aspects of a decision.

The shared F describes a way to weigh decisions. ESFJ’s dominant Fe takes account of shared values and how a decision affects people. INFP’s dominant Fi weighs the decision against values the person endorses. A value someone holds personally can also be shared by a group. Either person can be considerate and principled.

### ### ESFJ and INFP: weighing the same revision request

In a fictional editorial project, two editors receive the same email declining the current draft and suggesting a new opening. Both can review the same manuscript and reader feedback, both have the same deadline, and both can propose a revision.

One line of reasoning asks what the writer and readers agree the opening should accomplish, and looks for relevant feedback on earlier drafts. Another asks what idea the writer most wants to preserve and considers several ways to bring it forward. These illustrate Fe–Si and Fi–Ne in the model. The same editor can use both.

Either person could acknowledge the email or reread the draft first. A deadline or the need to clarify feedback can explain either choice. The order of actions cannot establish a type, even if it repeats across several messages.

### ### ESFJ and INFP: how Fe, Fi, Si and Ne fit into the stacks

Under the convention used here, ESFJ is Fe–Si–Ne–Ti and INFP is Fi–Ne–Si–Te. For ESFJ, J indicates an outward judging process, F identifies that process as Feeling, and E makes Fe dominant. For INFP, P indicates an outward perceiving process, N identifies it as Ne, and I makes that outward process auxiliary to inward-facing Fi.

The stacks show Si and Ne in each type, with the auxiliary and tertiary positions reversed under this convention. The Myers & Briggs Foundation also lists Ni as an option for ESFJ’s tertiary Intuition and Se for INFP’s tertiary Sensing. The stacks describe a theoretical model. They cannot show the order of someone’s actions. See the [ESFJ profile](/en/personality/esfj) and the [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp) for each set of preferences.
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
The same person can spot a problem in a draft and write a clear note about the next step. If two people share the work, divide it by responsibility, familiarity with the material and the time available.

### ### ESFJ and INFP: writing a revision note the author can use

In a fictional edit, an author has reordered the opening chronologically. Both editors can see that the central question now appears in the third paragraph. One way to approach the note is to recognise what the change improved and explain where readers may lose the thread. Another is to locate the central sentence and suggest two ways to retain it near the start. Either editor can do both.

A combined reply could say, “The new opening makes the timeline clear. Right now, readers don’t learn what the piece is trying to answer until paragraph three. Could we move the central question to the opening and keep the timeline that follows?” Ask a colleague whether they can explain the problem and name the next edit. That checks the note’s clarity and gives no evidence about either editor’s type.

### ### ESFJ and INFP: responding to a flatmate’s post

In a fictional shared flat, someone posts a general complaint about the kitchen. Two flatmates see the same message and have the same chore rota. Either could ask which task was left undone or check what each person agreed to do. Either can do both before offering to put things right.

Focus the conversation on what happened, who can do the outstanding task and how to handle it next time. Sending a message promptly or checking the rota beforehand can depend on who has time and what they already know. Neither choice tells you how much someone values the relationship.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
Fe and Fi describe different reference points for judgment. They cannot tell you who is kinder. Either type can account for other people’s needs and stand by a personal commitment.

E/I concerns the direction of attention and energy. Someone may speak at length when they know the topic and want quiet after a busy day. How they act in a single social setting is weak evidence about their preference.

An ESFJ can defend a decision and an INFP can change their mind when presented with new information. The preferences do not rank determination. The reasons and circumstances matter more than the fact someone changed their mind.

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Extraversion and Introversion describe where attention and energy tend to go. Sensing emphasises concrete details and experience, while Intuition emphasises patterns and possibilities. Judging and Perceiving describe a preference for structure or openness in the outside world. These differences concern separate aspects of a decision.

The shared F describes a way to weigh decisions. ESFJ’s dominant Fe takes account of shared values and how a decision affects people. INFP’s dominant Fi weighs the decision against values the person endorses. A value someone holds personally can also be shared by a group. Either person can be considerate and principled.

### ### ESFJ and INFP: weighing the same revision request

In a fictional editorial project, two editors receive the same email declining the current draft and suggesting a new opening. Both can review the same manuscript and reader feedback, both have the same deadline, and both can propose a revision.

One line of reasoning asks what the writer and readers agree the opening should accomplish, and looks for relevant feedback on earlier drafts. Another asks what idea the writer most wants to preserve and considers several ways to bring it forward. These illustrate Fe–Si and Fi–Ne in the model. The same editor can use both.

Either person could acknowledge the email or reread the draft first. A deadline or the need to clarify feedback can explain either choice. The order of actions cannot establish a type, even if it repeats across several messages.

### ### ESFJ and INFP: how Fe, Fi, Si and Ne fit into the stacks

Under the convention used here, ESFJ is Fe–Si–Ne–Ti and INFP is Fi–Ne–Si–Te. For ESFJ, J indicates an outward judging process, F identifies that process as Feeling, and E makes Fe dominant. For INFP, P indicates an outward perceiving process, N identifies it as Ne, and I makes that outward process auxiliary to inward-facing Fi.

The stacks show Si and Ne in each type, with the auxiliary and tertiary positions reversed under this convention. The Myers & Briggs Foundation also lists Ni as an option for ESFJ’s tertiary Intuition and Se for INFP’s tertiary Sensing. The stacks describe a theoretical model. They cannot show the order of someone’s actions. See the [ESFJ profile](/en/personality/esfj) and the [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp) for each set of preferences.
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
The same person can spot a problem in a draft and write a clear note about the next step. If two people share the work, divide it by responsibility, familiarity with the material and the time available.

### ### ESFJ and INFP: writing a revision note the author can use

In a fictional edit, an author has reordered the opening chronologically. Both editors can see that the central question now appears in the third paragraph. One way to approach the note is to recognise what the change improved and explain where readers may lose the thread. Another is to locate the central sentence and suggest two ways to retain it near the start. Either editor can do both.

A combined reply could say, “The new opening makes the timeline clear. Right now, readers don’t learn what the piece is trying to answer until paragraph three. Could we move the central question to the opening and keep the timeline that follows?” Ask a colleague whether they can explain the problem and name the next edit. That checks the note’s clarity and gives no evidence about either editor’s type.

### ### ESFJ and INFP: responding to a flatmate’s post

In a fictional shared flat, someone posts a general complaint about the kitchen. Two flatmates see the same message and have the same chore rota. Either could ask which task was left undone or check what each person agreed to do. Either can do both before offering to put things right.

Focus the conversation on what happened, who can do the outstanding task and how to handle it next time. Sending a message promptly or checking the rota beforehand can depend on who has time and what they already know. Neither choice tells you how much someone values the relationship.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
Fe and Fi describe different reference points for judgment. They cannot tell you who is kinder. Either type can account for other people’s needs and stand by a personal commitment.

E/I concerns the direction of attention and energy. Someone may speak at length when they know the topic and want quiet after a busy day. How they act in a single social setting is weak evidence about their preference.

An ESFJ can defend a decision and an INFP can change their mind when presented with new information. The preferences do not rank determination. The reasons and circumstances matter more than the fact someone changed their mind.

faq_blocks.answer:
In the model, Fe emphasises shared values and the effect on people, while Fi emphasises values a person has considered and endorsed. Either editor might draw on both perspectives.

In the same fictional edit, both can check where readers lose the thread and look for a way to preserve the author’s central point. Neither type can be identified by which part of the revision they do first.
faq_blocks.question: ### How might ESFJ and INFP consider the same revision request?

faq_blocks.answer:
Extraverted Feeling (Fe) evaluates a decision in relation to shared values and the people involved. Introverted Feeling (Fi) evaluates it in relation to values the person endorses. In Myers-Briggs type dynamics, Fe is dominant for ESFJ and Fi is dominant for INFP.

faq_blocks.question: ### What is the difference between ESFJ’s Fe and INFP’s Fi?

faq_blocks.answer:
Yes. A person can practise both approaches and choose what the circumstances call for.

Time needed to recover after a meeting can depend on workload, sleep, stress and familiarity with the task. It cannot tell you which function someone used or establish their type.
faq_blocks.question: ### Can an INFP manage a group discussion and an ESFJ hold their ground?

faq_blocks.answer:
Yes. Editing can involve finding a story, revising a draft and checking facts. Community work can involve answering questions, coordinating events and reviewing what members need. Training and experience matter in both roles.

Try writing revision notes and a plan for responding to readers using the same fictional project. Use the FermatMind Career Library to compare the tasks you would like to do repeatedly with the duties of actual roles.
faq_blocks.question: ### Can either type do editing or community work?

faq_blocks.answer:
Begin with something both can check. For example, point out where a paragraph repeats a claim, then ask what the writer wants readers to take from it.

Agree on what the revision needs to resolve before deciding which lines to move or cut. Either person can lead that conversation. Their role and knowledge of the material matter.

faq_blocks.answer:
Check whether you used the same questionnaire, scoring and language. Consider the situations you thought about when answering, including what those situations required of you.

sections.body_md:
If two results differ, compare the instrument, version, language and scoring. Think about the circumstances you used as reference points when answering. The results alone cannot tell you what caused the difference.

Choose several occasions where you had a genuine choice about how to give feedback. Note where your attention went, what information you used and what you wanted the feedback to accomplish. Then compare the situations and include an example where you used a different approach.

These notes can put words to your experience. They cannot determine your type, measure how near your score was to a cutoff or validate a test result.
sections.title: ESFJ and INFP: how to keep observing

items.answer:
In the model, Fe emphasises shared values and the effect on people, while Fi emphasises values a person has considered and endorsed. Either editor might draw on both perspectives.

In the same fictional edit, both can check where readers lose the thread and look for a way to preserve the author’s central point. Neither type can be identified by which part of the revision they do first.
items.question: ### How might ESFJ and INFP consider the same revision request?

items.answer:
Extraverted Feeling (Fe) evaluates a decision in relation to shared values and the people involved. Introverted Feeling (Fi) evaluates it in relation to values the person endorses. In Myers-Briggs type dynamics, Fe is dominant for ESFJ and Fi is dominant for INFP.

Both can support the same decision. Phrases such as “I think” or “we agree” can reflect someone’s role or speaking habits and are insufficient to establish their type.
items.question: ### What is the difference between ESFJ’s Fe and INFP’s Fi?

items.answer:
Yes. A person can practise both approaches and choose what the circumstances call for.

Time needed to recover after a meeting can depend on workload, sleep, stress and familiarity with the task. It cannot tell you which function someone used or establish their type.
items.question: ### Can an INFP manage a group discussion and an ESFJ hold their ground?

items.answer:
Yes. Editing can involve finding a story, revising a draft and checking facts. Community work can involve answering questions, coordinating events and reviewing what members need. Training and experience matter in both roles.

Try writing revision notes and a plan for responding to readers using the same fictional project. Use the FermatMind Career Library to compare the tasks you would like to do repeatedly with the duties of actual roles.
items.question: ### Can either type do editing or community work?

items.answer:
Begin with something both can check. For example, point out where a paragraph repeats a claim, then ask what the writer wants readers to take from it.

Agree on what the revision needs to resolve before deciding which lines to move or cut. Either person can lead that conversation. Their role and knowledge of the material matter.
items.question: ### How can ESFJ and INFP discuss a disagreement about a draft?

items.answer:
Check whether you used the same questionnaire, scoring and language. Consider the situations you thought about when answering, including what those situations required of you.

If the tool explains its E/I, S/N and J/P scores and cutoffs, use that guidance to interpret the difference. Reflect on choices from several comparable situations and include examples that challenge your first impression. A simple count cannot identify which result fits better.
